options: Clipper64 on integer coordinates: each case is scaled by 2^k (the smallest k in 0..60 that makes every ordinate an integer), which is exact for doubles, instead of the double API ClipperD/PathsD with a decimal precision
FillRule::EvenOdd (the API has no default fill rule; EvenOdd is correct for valid OGC input)
areas are measured by the adapter: exact shoelace over the output Paths64 (int128 products, 192-bit accumulator), rounded once, divided by 4^k

v2 overlay output: Execute into a PolyTree64 (outer nodes are shells, their children holes, a hole's children new polygons); each grid point is written as the double nearest to x * 2^-k (exact unless |x| > 2^53), rings as Clipper orients them, closed by the adapter

precision.grid: 2^-k, k the smallest integer in 0..60 that makes every ordinate of both operands an integer (--scale-bits B uses the largest k keeping every scaled ordinate below 2^B)
